statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42770 ("FFC-DH Peer Validation Uses Attacker-Supplied q", Low): when EVP_PKEY_derive_set_peer() is given an X9.42 (DHX) peer key, the peer key is checked for subgroup membership against the q carried in the peer key instead of the local q, so a malicious peer presenting a key with the victim's p and g and a chosen q can mount a small-subgroup attack against a long-lived static DHX key. OpenSSL fixed it in 3.5.7 (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt; fix on the openssl-3.5 branch: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/ca2237ab5615641b662183b077f62c08d75e8070, committed after OpenSSL 3.5.6). Alpine lists it fixed in openssl 3.5.7-r0 (https://security.alpinelinux.org/vuln/CVE-2026-42770). The advisory lists the OpenSSL FIPS modules, including 3.5 and 3.1.2, as affected as well. The DHI Alpine 3.23 openssl packages (origin openssl: libcrypto3, libssl3, openssl and its -dbg, -dev, -doc, -libs-static and -misc packages in the DHI Alpine repository, and openssl-fips in the DHI security repository) are published as 3.5.4-r0, 3.5.5-r0, 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, 3.5.6-r0, 3.5.6-r1, 3.5.7-r0, 3.5.7-r1, 3.5.8-r0, 3.5.8-r1, 3.5.9-r0, 3.5.9-r1 and 3.5.9-r2 (openssl-fips from 3.5.5_git20260330-r1 on), each for x86_64 and aarch64. The OpenSSL version string in libcrypto.so.3 (libcrypto3) and in fips.so (openssl-fips) of every build, read from packages verified against the index checksums, is the OpenSSL release in the package version. Every build before 3.5.7-r0, including 3.5.5_git20260330-r1, whose libcrypto reports OpenSSL 3.5.5, is based on OpenSSL 3.5.6 or older without the fix, and 3.5.7-r0 and every later build are based on OpenSSL 3.5.7 or later. The openssl-fips fips.so of each build is the FIPS provider from the same OpenSSL release, so it follows the same boundary. The separate openssl-provider-fips package (the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider) is a different source package and is not covered by this statement.

statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-42770 ("FFC-DH Peer Validation Uses Attacker-Supplied q", Low): when EVP_PKEY_derive_set_peer() is given an X9.42 (DHX) peer key, the peer key is checked for subgroup membership against the q carried in the peer key instead of the local q, so a malicious peer presenting a key with the victim's p and g and a chosen q can mount a small-subgroup attack against a long-lived static DHX key. OpenSSL fixed it in 3.5.7 (https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260609.txt; fix on the openssl-3.5 branch: https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/ca2237ab5615641b662183b077f62c08d75e8070, committed after OpenSSL 3.5.6). Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 (DSA-6335-1): https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-42770. The advisory lists the OpenSSL FIPS modules, including 3.5 and 3.1.2, as affected as well. The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI security repository (the FIPS builds and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build only in the security repository). The Debian changelog shipped in libssl3t64 was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64 (25 versions, packages verified against the index checksums). No build of Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-42770; the first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 entry naming it. The openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the same OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds. The fix is in the provider code that libcrypto and the 3.5 FIPS provider are both built from, so the non-FIPS builds of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and later are fixed. The FIPS builds pair that libcrypto with the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider, which the advisory lists as affected and which carries no fix, and their openssl.cnf (in the openssl package) sets default_properties = fips=yes, so key exchange is performed by that provider; every FIPS build is affected. Disassembly of dh_set_peer, located with the published debug symbols (libssl3t64-dbgsym and openssl-provider-fips-dbgsym, amd64 and arm64), confirms this: the q-comparison flag passed to the domain-parameter check is a constant in libcrypto.so.3 and the 3.5 fips.so of the rebuild of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, is derived from the local key's q in libcrypto.so.3 and the 3.5 fips.so of the rebuilds of 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 (FIPS builds' libcrypto included), and is still a constant in the 3.1.2 fips.so of the FIPS builds of 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. Each FIPS build sorts directly above the non-FIPS builds of the same Debian release, so the range reopens at the FIPS build of Debian 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1 and closes again at the next non-FIPS release. The status is AFFECTED because the newest FIPS build is still affected.
